subtitle: Native Loader lets you install native mods for Minecraft Dungeons II! Native mods are DLL files that run alongside the game, loaded from your ~mods folder when the game starts, without replacing any game files. A template for making your own native mods is available separately.
description:
Native Loader lets you install native mods for Minecraft Dungeons II!

Native mods are DLL files that run alongside the game. Native Loader loads every native mod in your ~mods folder when the game starts, without replacing any game files. On its own it does nothing, so you only need it for mods that say they require it.

Install

There are two files on this page. To play with mods, you only need Native Loader. Native Mod Template is only for making mods.

  1. Download the Native Loader file.
  2. Close the game, and fully close the Minecraft Launcher if you use it.
  3. Open your Minecraft Dungeons II binaries folder.
    • Steam: Right click the game in your library, then Manage > Browse local files, then open Dungeons\Binaries\Win64
    • Minecraft Launcher: C:\XboxGames\Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Binaries\WinGDK
    If you picked a different install folder in the Minecraft Launcher, it is Minecraft Dungeons II\Content\Dungeons\Binaries\WinGDK inside that folder.
  4. Open the zip and move winmm.dll into the Win64 or WinGDK folder from step 3, next to the game's exe.

Native mods go in their own folders inside ~mods, the same as other mods. Each mod's readme says where its files go.

Antivirus

Windows Defender may flag winmm.dll as Contebrew.A!ml. This is a false positive caused by how mod loaders work: winmm.dll sits next to the game, passes everything through to the real Windows winmm.dll, and loads your mods. It has been reported to Microsoft.

If Defender removes it, restore it from Windows Security > Virus & threat protection > Protection history.

Uninstall

Delete winmm.dll from the Win64 or WinGDK folder. Native mods in ~mods stop loading without it.

Making mods

Download the Native Mod Template file to make your own native mods. It includes two example mods, each in C, C++ and Rust, with build scripts, and a readme covering how mods are loaded, the debug console, logging, and functions that Blueprint Loader mods can call.
